strengths: Well-motivated problem: Addresses parameter-dependent physical constraints without paired training data, which is practically important for scientific applications
Principled theoretical foundation: Reformulation as stochastic optimal control via adjoint matching is mathematically sound; weak-form residuals are numerically stable and practical
Clever architectural design: Joint evolution of states and parameters using surrogate base flow from inverse predictor is sensible; parameter regularization (λf) provides useful trade-off
Extensive implementation details: Comprehensive appendices with hyperparameters, test functions, and heuristics support reproducibility
Diverse task coverage: Experiments span multiple scenarios (denoising, guidance, super-resolution, boundary enforcement) on two PDE systems
weaknesses: Limited novelty: Core contribution is applying existing adjoint-matching framework to PDE residuals as reward; joint parameter evolution is straightforward engineering rather than conceptual advance

Weak experimental validation: Only one weak/unfair baseline (ECI); no quantitative comparison with PBFM, PINNs, or other physics-constrained methods; limited to 2 canonical PDEs with modest datasets (10K-20K samples)

Unvalidated inverse problem claims: Parameter recovery accuracy barely quantified; no held-out test set validation; guidance experiments are conditioning tasks, not ill-posed inverse problems; quality bounded by inverse predictor φ's accuracy

Problematic experimental setup: Results use σ(t)=0 (no test-time noise) contradicting denoising claims; adaptive tail refinement provides unfair computational advantage; inverse predictor trained on base samples creates circularity

Insufficient ablations: No systematic comparison with naive alternatives (post-hoc parameter prediction); limited analysis of λf-λx tradeoff; no sensitivity study for test function design; many hyperparameters appear manually tuned

Methodological concerns: No principled approach for setting λf and λx; memoryless noise schedule heuristic lacks justification; parameter normalization effect not shown; mollifier form appears arbitrary

Limited scope and generalization: Both PDEs share similar structure (coefficient fields in elliptic/hyperbolic equations); no complex systems, coupled PDEs, time-varying parameters, or real-world validation; all inverse problems infer single coefficient field

Presentation issues: Figure 1 appears twice with identical caption but different content; dense notation in joint evolution section; limited intuition for design choices; missing comparison with concurrent PBFM work

strengths: Well-motivated problem: genuinely addresses the gap of enforcing parameter-dependent PDE constraints without paired training data, with high practical relevance for scientific discovery

Technically sound approach: clever joint parameter-state evolution formulation using the inverse predictor as surrogate base flow; weak-form residuals with random test functions provide numerically stable learning signals
Lemma 1 extends adjoint matching theory meaningfully: scaled noise schedule σ²(t)=(1-κ)2ηt generalizes memoryless property while providing practical numerical stability

Exceptionally comprehensive experiments: four diverse PDE systems (elliptic, hyperbolic, parabolic, saddle-point), systematic ablations (Base AM, Base AM+φ, joint model), realistic conditions (misspecification, noise), multiple metrics (weak/strong residuals, MMD, diversity), cross-domain validation (natural images)

Excellent reproducibility: detailed datasets, architectures, hyperparameters, full training algorithms, promised code release, extensive non-curated samples; practical efficiency (15 min–2 hours on single GPU)

Clear practical utility: enables sampling with sparse observations via guidance, preserves diversity while improving physics compliance (controllable trade-offs via λf), works with low-fidelity noisy data
Strong presentation with clear motivation and well-designed figures showing residual-distribution trade-offs
weaknesses: Limited core novelty: primarily applies existing adjoint matching framework (Domingo-Enrich et al. 2025) to new setting; weak-form residuals standard in scientific computing; joint parameter evolution clever but somewhat incremental—using inverse predictor for surrogate flows is pragmatic but not deeply novel

Insufficient Bayesian inverse problem validation: claims to solve ill-posed inverse problems but lacks rigorous posterior inference and uncertainty quantification; parameter accuracy evaluated indirectly via residuals/MMD rather than direct comparison to ground truth; no comparison with dedicated inverse problem solvers (MCMC, variational inference) or Bayesian approaches

Experimental comparisons could be stronger: PBFM comparison acknowledged as unfair (different problem settings); limited inference-time baselines beyond ECI; no comparison with classifier-guided diffusion or other guidance methods; base FM deliberately trained with misspecified physics, creating artificial conditions

Hyperparameter sensitivity and design choices: method introduces numerous hyperparameters (λx, λα, λf, κ, q, Klast, K, LCT); full sensitivity landscape unclear; regularization term f(α) appears necessary to prevent distribution shift, suggesting base method limitations; test function design (Wendland wavelets) lacks sensitivity analysis; heuristic modifications to ηt and time grids reduce theoretical elegance

Limited parameter diversity: all experiments use spatially varying coefficient fields (permeability, modulus, sound speed, viscosity); missing scalar parameters, boundary values, discontinuous parameters; scalability to higher-dimensional parameter spaces unclear

Dependence on inverse predictor quality without robustness analysis: entire framework relies on pre-trained φ; no analysis of how φ quality affects results; in practice, learning α when paired data is scarce may be as hard as original problem

Theoretical gaps: no convergence analysis of fine-tuning procedure; no formal justification for why joint evolution improves parameter recovery; connection between tilted distributions and inverse problem solving could be more rigorous

Experimental design limitations: reference datasets Dref are synthetic/clean, known ground-truth PDEs—in practice, true PDE unknown; scalability to resolutions beyond 64×64 unclear; evaluation metrics somewhat circular (scaled by Dref residuals)

Limited failure mode analysis: Stokes with severe misspecification (F₀=2.0→0.0) produces large residuals; insufficient discussion of when method fails; robustness to chaotic/multistable systems unexplored
Presentation: natural image experiment (Section 4.6) feels disconnected from PDE applications; key details (guidance) relegated to appendix; Figure 1 has small text and complex layout
